title: 'Police break into volunteer’s house at 1am, thrash him, misbehave with wife': CJP

CJP is focusing on concerns about voter exclusion and alleged vote theft in upcoming demonstrations.

title: Woman given wrong blood after accident; hospital's unusual defence fails before panel
content: In a shocking incident in Chhattisgarh, Madhu Khakha faced a grave medical error when she was mistakenly given AB-positive blood during her treatment instead of her correct B-positive type. This blunder triggered severe complications, leading to a delay in her surgery. Subsequently, a consumer commission deemed the hospital negligent, awarding her compensation for both her distress and legal fees, highlighting the grave risks associated with incompatible blood transfusions.

title: Railways cancel several Mail/Express trains reaching New Delhi, Nizamuddin on Oct 10
content: On October 10, all Mail and Express trains arriving at New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin will be canceled. This decision is due to the anticipated severe traffic congestion around these railway stations. The cancellations affect trains scheduled between 4am and 2pm on that day. Additionally, trains departing after 2pm on October 10 are also canceled if they arrive during the mentioned timeframe.

title: 21-year-old raises over $146,000 for 80-year-old AMC usher in under 24 hours
content: A 21-year-old woman in Tennessee raised more than $146,000 in less than 24 hours for an 80-year-old AMC cinema worker after noticing her cleaning up rubbish. Brooklyn Green initially hoped to collect $500 through TikTok and GoFundMe. The elderly worker, Mary, who has worked in theatres for over 45 years, later thanked donors and requested that the fundraiser be paused.

title: Teen hiker used AI to plan route, stranded on cliff and rescued by helicopter
content: A 16-year-old hiker in Canada was rescued by helicopter after becoming stranded on a steep cliff on Crown Mountain in British Columbia. The teenager had used Claude AI to help plan his route but wandered onto a dangerous climbing path. Rescuers reached him using ropes and a helicopter, later warning hikers against relying entirely on AI for navigation.

title: Sridhar Vembu to Indians working in US: Come back; America no longer needs us
content: Sridhar Vembu emphasized the contributions of Indians to America's technology sector amid increasing immigration uncertainties. He urged Indians living in the US to consider returning home to build India's future. Vembu highlighted the personal difficulties faced by visa holders in the US who have established their lives there. He reflected on the broader political landscape affecting Indian professionals abroad and echoed a sense of urgency for repatriation.

title: 'Youth are no longer scared of you, PM Modi; will march to Jantar Mantar': Abhijeet Dipke

title: 'Bas lage rhna hai': Back in rhythm, Mukesh Kumar pushes for India comeback
content: After more than two years out of the Indian team, Mukesh Kumar is back on the selectors’ radar following his selection for India A’s tour of New Zealand. The Bengal pacer discusses rediscovering his rhythm, improving his fitness and seam position, managing the demands of a packed cricket calendar, and his determination to fight his way back into the national setup.

title: Delays of several hours: Passenger trains using slower freight locos amid shortage
content: Indian Railways records  contain several instances in which a lack of locomotives designed for passenger services led to trains being hauled by freight engines, which operate at lower speeds. The use of these locomotives has affected running times and caused operational delays, the records show. The Railway Ministry, however, said it was accelerating efforts to expand locomotive production.

title: Rs 2 cr deposit, no ITR, Rs 2.51 cr addition; ITAT quashes case due to 5 day delay

title: Shannen Doherty’s Malibu home bought for $2.56m sells for $7.65m

This five-bedroom residence was a refuge for Doherty during her courageous fight against cancer. Following the severe damage from the Woolsey Fire in 2018, significant renovations restored its charm and elevated its desirability.

title: UK girl gave dad £500 to build mushroom house; it later won Shed of the Year

Ben Swanborough created a two-storey hideaway featuring a trapdoor, stained-glass windows, a glass floor overlooking a stream and a glass roof for stargazing. Ali recalled how Patekar supported him during difficult times, including his mother's illness and his own health issues. Tributes from the Pakistani cricket fraternity, including Umar Akmal, honored Patekar's legacy and contributions.

title: Can a warship become a mini aircraft carrier? India, US are testing two different answers

The systems will enhance intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance for naval operations and support various missions. The Indian drones aim for at least 60% indigenous content and face operational challenges from the maritime environment. Meanwhile, the United States is developing advanced AI-piloted drones for naval warfare without requiring a runway.

content: The joy of silly words captivates children as they anticipate the playful sounds, fostering laughter and social interaction. While adults might not share this enthusiasm for long, children revel in these exchanges that nurture vital communication skills. Through these interactions, they not only express preferences but also enhance their vocabulary, paving the way for meaningful language development during these formative years.

title: J&K: PDP leader detained after calling terrorist Burhan Wani a 'martyr'
content:
NEW DELHI: PDP leader Abdul Kabir referred to Hizbul Mujahideen terrorist Burhan Wani as a "martyr" during a speech at an event in Jammu and Kashmir. He was later detained in Kishtwar for questioning over the remark. Earlier, news agency ANI asked Kabir about his use of the term "martyr" for the slain terrorist. He said, "I had stated that when Burhan Wani was killed, BJP leaders visited his home and provided compensation. It is our freedom to decide whether or not to call him a martyr. We live in a democratic country. This is my personal view." Burhan Wani was 21 when he was killed by security forces in Kokernag in Anantnag district. He was a posterboy of the Hizbul Mujahideen terrorist group.

End of Article

title: Supreme Court rejects plea seeking free hand for Delhi Police to deal with protesters
content:
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has rejected a plea seeking directions to give the Delhi Police a free hand to deal with protesters, observing that the future of young students and their families must be kept in mind while considering such matters. A bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said many of the protesters were young and should not be unnecessarily entangled in prolonged court proceedings. “These are young students and protesters before us. We have to see their parents, we have to see they have a long life. [They should not be] entangled with court hearings etc.,” the CJI said. The court, however, clarified that its earlier orders protecting protesters did not extend to those alleged to be hardened criminals or accused of serious offences.

End of Article
